title: Theranos died in 2018. Who JUST renewed its Patents... and WHY?
summary: Theranos closed in 2018, yet someone paid to renew its Health Shield patent in April 2026. The trail runs through Fortress and Labrador Diagnostics.
description:
Previously on As the Lab Turns: Theranos died in 2018. Its patent never got the memo.

IN THIS EPISODE: a 19-year-old with a health monitor you swallow. A bird flu plan nobody ran past the chickens. And a "Health Shield" with a familiar-sounding quarantine, granted 6 years BEFORE Covid.

Then, years after the funeral, somebody pays Theranos' patent bills.

Who? And why?

THE PRINTED ISSUE
SIDE EYE: The Loser's Issue (Issue 1) is in print. Includes pages. None require a finger prick.
Get it on Amazon: https://a.co/d/02FwgFhM (or search "side eye magazine")

ONE QUESTION FOR THE COMMENTS
What should the unsigned card on Health Shield's renewal payment say? Rule: write it as a soap opera secret admirer. No names, because the record doesn't have one.

THE FILES WE KEPT
- US 8,862,448 (Health Shield), granted Oct 2014, plus its paid-up sisters 9,460,263; 11,139,084; 11,158,429; 11,195,624
- USPTO assignment records: Theranos IP Company, pledged to Fortress Credit Corp. (Dec 2017), renamed Labrador Diagnostics (March 2020)
- USPTO maintenance-fee record: Health Shield's 12th-year fee, paid April 1, 2026
- Labrador Diagnostics LLC v. BioFire Diagnostics (D. Del. 1:20-cv-00348), asserting US 8,283,155 and 10,533,994
- Labrador's March 16, 2020 press release: "an entity owned by investment funds managed by Fortress"

SIDE EYE. History, allegedly.

#Theranos #ElizabethHolmes #SideEye

transcript.text: Theranos is dead. This patent isn't.
Elizabeth Holmes and three co-inventors filed it in 2009: a plan to track disease across a whole country.
Theranos closed in 2018.
Nobody told the patent.
In April 2026, somebody paid to keep it alive.
2003. Holmes is 19.
She and her co-inventors file for a drug-dosing monitor.
One version, you swallow.
2006: a bird flu warning system, for "health and government officials." Samples from "the human, poultry and wild birds." The chickens were not consulted.
October 2009: Health Shield.
It's built as "a national health shield."
In one version, the analysis goes to officials, "not to individual users."
You might still get a quarantine notice.
Your contacts from "the past few days, weeks, months, or years" get notified.
Years.
"Quarantined in the whole neighborhood" is in the claims, the part the patent actually protects. Claim 15 reads like a shopping list.
Household quarantine. School closure.
Travel restrictions. Masks.
Health Shield was granted in October 2014.
Four inventors are named on it.
One of them, Ian Gibbons, died in May 2013.
December 2017: the patents move into a new company and get pledged to a lender, Fortress.
March 2020: that company becomes Labrador Diagnostics.
Four days later, it sues BioFire, maker of the COVID test.
Different patents. Health Shield sat this one out.
One of them was 55 days old.
Labrador said it wasn't about COVID testing, and dropped the case by June.
Same press release: Labrador is "an entity owned by investment funds managed by" Fortress.
March 24, 2026: one of the patents they sued with reaches the end of its term.
April 1, 2026: somebody paid Health Shield's final renewal fee.
Eight days apart.
The company's gone. The Shield paid up.
No record shows any government ever bought it.
It's a patent. It doesn't build itself.
It does have company.
Five Health Shield patents, all paid up.
Three of the patents were granted during the fraud trial.
